---
title: "MusicXML"
---

This page is executable:
every code block below runs when the documentation is built.

`openmusickit.io.musicxml` reads a MusicXML file into an `OmkGraph`
and writes a `Score` of a graph back out.
It reads `.musicxml`, `.xml` and compressed `.mxl` files,
partwise (what notation programs export),
and writes MusicXML 4.0.
It needs nothing beyond the standard library.

```{python}
import io
import tempfile
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import openmusickit as omk
from openmusickit.io.musicxml import canonicalize, compare, read, write
from openmusickit.io.musicxml.container import load
from openmusickit.systems import wsmn
from openmusickit.systems.wsmn.symbols import *
```

## Reading a file

`read` takes a path or a binary stream and returns a new graph holding one `Score`.
Here is a lead sheet from the test fixtures,
a Sibelius export of the New Orleans tune *Second Line*.

```{python}
lead_sheet = Path("../tests/scores/second-line-joe-avery/SECOND LINE, (THE ORIGINAL) (JOE AVERY BLUES).xml")

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always", omk.OmkWarning)
    graph = read(lead_sheet)

score = next(graph.nodes(omk.Score))
print(score.title)
print(score.composer)
print([part.name for part in graph.score_parts(score)])
```

The reader records what the file says and nothing more.
Each part is a `Part` performing a line
(a part on two staves performs a `LineGroup` of two lines).
Key, meter and clef are context events at the head of the line,
every bar line is a `DivisionEvent`,
ties and slurs are `MarkSpanner`s,
and a second voice is a line branched from the note it starts under.

```{python}
(part,) = graph.score_parts(score)
(stint,) = graph.stints(part)
melody = graph.spanner_start(stint)
for event in list(graph.walk_line(melody))[:9]:
    print(event if isinstance(event, (omk.NoteEvent, omk.DivisionEvent)) else type(event).__name__)
```

Chord symbols become a line of `ChordEvent`s with no duration,
each pinned to the note it stands over;
a timing walk from the melody finds them.

```{python}
(chord_head,) = (h for h in graph.score_lines(score) if isinstance(h, omk.ChordEvent))
onsets = graph.onsets(melody)
for chord in list(graph.walk_line(chord_head))[:5]:
    print(onsets[chord.id].rational_length, chord.chord)
```

Anything the reader cannot place
(an element with no home in the model yet, a word it does not know)
is not dropped silently:
it is an `OmkWarning`, counted by kind.
Presentation (layout, stems, beams, fonts, positions) is dropped without a warning:
that is not loss of music.

```{python}
for warning in caught:
    print(warning.message)
```

## Writing a file

`write` writes the graph's only Score
(pass `score=` when a graph holds several);
a target ending in `.mxl` is compressed.
`OmkGraph.from_file` and `export_file` do the same by suffix.

```{python}
out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore", omk.OmkWarning)
    write(graph, out / "second-line.musicxml")
    graph.export_file(out / "second-line.mxl")
    again = omk.OmkGraph.from_file(out / "second-line.mxl")

print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
print(again.is_equivalent(graph))
```

The writer is the reader's inverse:
what the reader built, written and read back, is the same music
(`is_equivalent` compares the graphs node for node, ids and metadata aside).

## Writing a graph built by hand

A graph does not need to come from a file.
A line needs no bar lines:
the meter in force places them,
and a note that crosses one is split and tied.
Here a melody in 3/4 is written with only a final bar line,
and its third note, a half note on the third beat, crosses the first.

```{python}
tune = omk.OmkGraph(omk.GraphMeta())
pitches = "E4 D4 C4 D4 E4 E4 E4".split()
rhythm = [quarter, quarter, half, quarter, quarter, quarter, half]
line = [
    omk.ModalContextEvent(modal_context=wsmn.Key.of(C, Major)),
    omk.MeterEvent(meter=three_four),
    omk.ClefEvent(clef=treble_clef),
    *(omk.NoteEvent(tones={wsmn.TonalVector.from_string(p)}, duration=d) for p, d in zip(pitches, rhythm)),
    omk.DivisionEvent(shape=final_bar),
]
tune.add_line(line)
title = omk.Score(title="Three bars", composer="Anon.")
flute = omk.Part(name="Flute")
tune.add_line_to_score(title, line[0])
tune.add_part_to_score(title, flute)
tune.add_stint(flute, omk.Stint(), line[0])

buffer = io.BytesIO()
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always", omk.OmkWarning)
    write(tune, buffer)
print([str(w.message) for w in caught])

from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET

for measure in ET.fromstring(buffer.getvalue()).iter("measure"):
    notes = [
        n.findtext("pitch/step") + n.findtext("pitch/octave") + " " + n.findtext("type")
        + "".join(f" (tie {t.get('type')})" for t in n.findall("tie"))
        for n in measure.iter("note")
    ]
    print(measure.get("number"), ", ".join(notes))
```

Read back, the line has a bar line wherever the meter put one,
and the half note that crossed the first is two notes joined by a tie.

```{python}
back = read(io.BytesIO(buffer.getvalue()))
head = next(back.score_lines(next(back.nodes(omk.Score))))
print([type(e).__name__ for e in back.walk_line(head) if not isinstance(e, omk.NoteEvent)])
print(sum(s.mark is tie for s in back.nodes(omk.MarkSpanner)), "tie")
```

The writer refuses only when there is nothing to write
(no Score, several and none chosen, a Score with no parts);
everything else it cannot write it leaves out with a warning:
an event of unknown or clock-time duration and the rest of its line,
a tone with no octave, an annotation, a line no part performs.

`omit` leaves out nodes by type, with whatever hangs from them,
without changing the graph: here, the chord symbols of the lead sheet.

```{python}
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore", omk.OmkWarning)
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    write(graph, buffer, omit=[omk.ChordEvent])
print(b"<harmony" in buffer.getvalue())
```

## Comparing documents

Did an export keep the music?
`canonicalize` reduces a MusicXML document to what it says musically:
every measure a list of items at explicit positions,
with presentation, `<divisions>`, voice and span numbers
and the order of voices in a measure normalized away.
`compare` lists the differences between two canonical forms by kind.
The lead sheet as Sibelius wrote it and as OMK writes it are the same music:

```{python}
original = canonicalize(load(lead_sheet))
written = canonicalize(load(out / "second-line.musicxml"))
print(compare(original, written))
```

A change to the music is a difference of its kind,
with the measure and part where it is.

```{python}
changed = (out / "second-line.musicxml").read_text().replace("<step>F</step>", "<step>G</step>", 1)
for difference in compare(written, canonicalize(load(io.BytesIO(changed.encode()))))[:2]:
    print(difference.kind, difference.measure, difference.detail)
```

## What is not kept

- **Layout and engraving.**
  Page and system breaks, positions, stems, beams, fonts, colours, credits:
  a written file is laid out by whatever program opens it.
- **Playback.**
  `<sound>`, MIDI settings (kept in the Part's metadata, not used).
- **Not yet modelled.**
  Control flow (repeats are bar-line shapes; endings and % bars are recorded but not followed),
  gradual tempo changes as spans, figured bass, drum maps.

What the writer needs to put a file back as it was
and the model cannot hold
(voice and measure numbers, hidden notes, tuplet brackets, part ids, instruments)
is kept in each node's `meta["musicxml"]`, a dict OMK itself never reads.
The `reader` module's docstring lists its keys.

## Reviewing an export

For checking the writer against real scores,
`tests/scores/review.py` sets each fixture's original engraving
beside MuseScore's engraving of the export
and writes the canonical differences:

```bash
uv run python -m tests.scores.review second-line-joe-avery
```

The pages land in `_review/<fixture>/`.
It needs MuseScore (`mscore`), Poppler's `pdftoppm`,
and for the side-by-side images ImageMagick's `montage`.
